Twenty-two years of structuring became a method that every new mandate starts from.

HAYKALAH does not start a mandate from a blank page. Since 2004, more than 650 engagements have been turned into one deliverable chain, a set of domain playbooks, a screening matrix and a commercial model that has moved from fee to equity. This page explains how the method works, the six ways it creates value for clients, and where Shariah approval and regulated activities sit within it.

Strategic architects of Value.

What we do

  • One deliverable chain, reused for 22 years.

  • Domain playbooks for the sectors we know in depth.

  • HOAM, the HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix.

  • Technology-backed delivery, measured from day one.

  • A commercial model that moved from fee to equity.

  • A compounding loop that feeds each new mandate.

Six ways we create value

These six describe what HAYKALAH does for clients. They are different from the four knowledge eras in the compounding loop below (Accumulate, Commercialize, Monetize, Utilize), which trace how HAYKALAH’s own know-how was built.

  1. 01

    Innovation

    We design the structure a deal needs, even when no template exists.

    New Shariah-compliant instruments, vehicles, operating models and digital tools, designed for the mandate in hand.

    In practice

    • Shariah-compliant products and capital instruments.
    • New vehicles: DevCo/ProjectCo consortiums and the waqf-manager model.
    • Technology and AI that automate routine work and support human judgment.
  2. 02

    Monetization

    We turn assets that cost money to hold into recurring income and capital.

    Idle land, buildings and facilities become income, refinancing capacity and capital to recycle.

    In practice

    • The engine: Audit → Optimize → Structure → Operate → Monetize.
    • Raw land to an income-producing asset.
    • Refinancing and capital recycling.
  3. 03

    Optimization

    We test every option before capital is committed, then choose the best use, cost and control.

    Highest-and-best-use studies, capital stacks weighed for cost, control and clarity, and competitive bank terms.

    In practice

    • Highest-and-best-use studies.
    • Capital structures optimized for cost, control and clarity.
    • Competing lender offers, compared like for like.
  4. 04

    Automation

    We automate reporting, records and routine operations, so people spend their time on judgment.

    AI reporting dashboards, ERP, CRM and workflow automation, and digital records with a full audit trail.

    In practice

    • AI reporting dashboards with live KPIs for investors, boards and operators.
    • ERP, CRM and workflow automation that removes manual steps and lowers the cost to serve.
    • Under-used assets automated to generate revenue, with integrated AI-based reporting.
    • Asset-performance monitoring with sensor data.
  5. 05

    Transformation

    We change how an organization, an asset or a portfolio works, from governance to data.

    Governance, operating models, data rooms and AI dashboards that let decisions keep pace with capital.

    In practice

    • Family governance and holding structures.
    • Digital records, data rooms and AI dashboards.
    • Operating-model change for government entities and their assets.
  6. 06

    Commercialization

    We take ideas, knowledge and public assets to market with a business model, an operator and paying users.

    Business models, operating companies and go-to-market plans that turn concepts into revenue.

    In practice

    • Venture building: advise → build → operate → exit.
    • Commercial blueprints for public and cultural assets.
    • Commercializing knowledge economies and research-linked ventures.

How we work

Every era of the archive shows the same chain: MR → FS → FM → VR → BP → BD → IM/PPM → TS → DD → Implementation. Each step answers one question.

  1. MR Market research Is there demand, and at what price?
  2. FS Feasibility study Does the project work technically and financially?
  3. FM Financial model What are the cash flows, returns and funding needs under each scenario?
  4. VR Valuation report What is the asset or company worth?
  5. BP Business plan How will the company operate and grow?
  6. BD Banking document Is it bankable, and on what terms?
  7. IM/PPM Information or private placement memorandum What are investors offered, and on what risks?
  8. TS Term sheet What are the commercial terms?
  9. DD Due diligence What could go wrong?
  10. Implementation Implementation and operation Who forms, operates and monitors the company?

Domain playbooks

Where the record runs deep, the chain became a playbook:

  • Holy Cities land-to-asset

    central-area land assembly with in-kind equity, pilgrim-demand modeling and hotel rate studies.

  • Mashaer pricing and financing

    seasonal revenue, per-pilgrim pricing, and capex for tents and utilities.

  • DevCo/ProjectCo consortium architecture

    pooling land from many owners, allocating risk, and PSP Law consortium rules.

  • FINA. Sukuk and fund templates

    asset-backed Sukuk, Ijara, Istisna’a, Wakala and fund terms.

  • The waqf-manager model

    waqf establishment, nazir governance and income distribution. NATHARAH, a HAYKALAH venture, is built on it.

  • Healthcare NewCo and capital-raising playbook

    bed-based economics, operator partnerships and offering design.

  • Industrial feasibility and project-finance pack

    project finance, engineering partners and offtake.

  • Institutional co-founder terms

    company formation, staged gates and equity-for-build, screened with HOAM.

HOAM

HOAM, the HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix, scores each new opportunity on six axes and compares it with two decades of precedent, so that screening is fast and comparable from one deal to the next. In 2025–26, HOAM was used to score 14 fintech and fund deals for a fintech fund platform. HOAM is a screening tool, not investment advice.

Technology-backed delivery

Each structure runs on a five-step loop: Optimize → Measure → Improve → Record → Correct. AI reporting dashboards, ERP and CRM automation, asset-performance monitoring and data rooms give owners one source of truth, and variance alerts trigger action early. Each mandate keeps one data room and one model of record, and data protection is designed in from the start under the PDPL.

Illustrative operating model. Savings and efficiency gains vary by project and are not guaranteed.

From fee to equity

The commercial model has changed with the record:

  1. 2007–12

    retainer and success fee.

  2. 2013–19

    board seats and principal ventures.

  3. 2020–23

    implementation mandates, in which HAYKALAH stays through company formation.

  4. 2024–26

    equity-for-build, partner equity vesting at gates, fees deferred into project equity, and DevCo stakes.

We are not choosing between advisory and ownership. We are using advisory and execution to create the value.

The compounding loop

  1. 650+ engagements
  3. reusable playbooks
  5. faster, lower-risk execution
  7. stronger relationships
  9. the next mandate

The know-how was built in four overlapping eras: Accumulate (2004–12), Commercialize (2008–16), Monetize (2014–22) and Utilize (2023 to today). The archive also taught five lessons that we apply from day one: bring anchor capital to the mandate, price conditions precedent at the start, keep one model of record, track outcomes, and repeat the advise → build → exit cycle where it works.

Shariah approval

HAYKALAH designs Shariah-compliant structures, such as Sukuk, Ijara, Istisna’a, Musataha, Wakala and Waqf. HAYKALAH does not maintain its own Shariah board. Each structure is reviewed and approved by the Shariah board of the issuer, fund or financial institution involved; where a client has none, HAYKALAH can arrange an independent Shariah board for the transaction. No structure is final until that approval is given.

Regulated activities

HAYKALAH is a Saudi advisory and structuring house registered under Commercial Registration No. 7014123751. HAYKALAH is not an Authorised Person of the Capital Market Authority. Where a transaction involves securities business regulated by the CMA, such as arranging, dealing, managing or advising on securities, or establishing or managing an investment fund, that activity is carried out by a CMA-authorised institution engaged for the transaction. Nothing on this website is an offer, a solicitation or investment advice.

Regulated activities are executed through appropriately licensed partners.

Questions

What is HOAM?

The HAYKALAH Opportunity Assessment Matrix. It scores a new opportunity on six axes and compares it with two decades of precedent. It is a screening tool, not investment advice.

Does HAYKALAH have its own Shariah board?

No. Each structure is approved by the Shariah board of the issuer, fund or financial institution involved. Where a client has none, HAYKALAH can arrange an independent Shariah board for the transaction.

Is HAYKALAH regulated by the Capital Market Authority?

HAYKALAH is not an Authorised Person of the CMA. Securities business and investment-fund activities in a transaction are carried out by a CMA-authorised institution engaged for that transaction.

What is equity-for-build?

A model in which HAYKALAH takes part of its reward as equity in the company or project it builds, vesting at agreed milestones, instead of fees alone.
